claim.why_it_matters: In 14.9.40.3 SUBTRACT general rules 1 and 2 the subscripts 1, 2, n on operand-1 are flattened into the operand name, so 'operand-11' and 'operand-12' read as operands eleven and twelve instead of the first and second occurrences of operand-1; the arithmetic-expression equivalence that defines the initial evaluation is garbled.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 601 (PDF p625), 14.9.40.3 GR1 and GR2: the expressions are printed '(operand-1 sub1 + operand-1 sub2 + ... + operand-1 sub n)' and '(operand-2 – (operand-1 sub1 + operand-1 sub2 + ... + operand-1 sub n))' with 1, 2, n as visibly lowered subscripts. page-625.md lines 27 and 39 read 'operand-11 + operand-12 + ... + operand-1n', the subscripts flattened into the name. The claim quotes both sources accurately. The flattening makes the text name nonexistent operands 'operand-11'/'operand-12' instead of the 1st/2nd occurrences of operand-1, a genuine content loss in the rule text. The surrounding prose ('the values of operand-1 are the values of literal-1 and ... identifier-1 in the order ... specified') lets a careful reader recover the meaning, so the practical impact is limited, but the transcribed expression itself is wrong.
